clue.text: On Tuesday, he died amid gunfire after beginning to burgle house

indicators.note: the gunfire-and-death part comes after the burglar's opening letter
the beginning of the word burgle supplies its opening letter
the Tuesday-and-death letters sit in the middle of the gunfire

parts.note: ack-ack is anti-aircraft fire, from old signallers' alphabet
OB is short for Latin obiit, 'he died', seen on gravestones

explanation.surface: A crime report: a householder killed in a shootout on Tuesday after a burglary began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he died' is the Latin obiit of old gravestones; 'house' is the definition, not part of the crime. 'On' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A back-to-back is a terraced house built sharing its rear wall with another, common in northern English industrial towns.

clue.text: Dunkirk veterans turn up underneath cloud

indicators.note: in a down entry the reversed piece sits below the veterans' letters

parts.note: the British Expeditionary Force, BEF, was evacuated from Dunkirk in 1940

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: a turn in a game is a go

explanation.surface: Old soldiers of Dunkirk appearing beneath a darkening sky.
explanation.definitionFit: To cloud something is to obscure or blur it, the sense of fog spread over it.

clue.text: In America, say, black woman has support from New Statesman

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece is underneath

parts.note: black is an example of a colour, spelt the American way without the u
Ada is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A black woman in America finds backing from a well-known political magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Statesman' reads as the British magazine, but 'Statesman' alone is the definition: a man of a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Read cryptically, a state's man is a native of Colorado, one of the American states.

clue.text: For shift, doctor sat in for matron

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hospital rota: a doctor filled in for the matron on her shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a person but is the verb that rearranges SAT IN FOR MATRON.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift is a change from one state to another, a conversion or metamorphosis.

clue.text: Refuse to engage with son too much, having caught cold

indicators.note: the son-and-excess letters close round the cold letter as if catching it

parts.note: a son is a boy
OTT is 'over the top', excessive
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A parent avoids the son, who overdoes things and has picked up a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: To shun or blacklist a firm or event is to refuse all dealings with it.

clue.text: Conservative has proposals for treasury

parts.note: C abbreviates the Conservative party
offers are proposals put forward

explanation.surface: A Tory politician brings forward plans for the Treasury.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffers are the funds or strongboxes of an organisation, its store of money.

clue.text: Tradesmen finally leaving brand new flat

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of the remaining letters
that letter departs from the word brand
the final letter of the word tradesmen is the one used

explanation.surface: Workmen finish up and depart from a brand-new apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes N, the last of Tradesmen, out of BRAND, and 'new' rearranges BRAD. 'flat' looks like an apartment but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat in the sense of dull or lifeless matches something dreary and colourless.

clue.text: Managed to squeeze down inside tree

indicators.note: the managed word squeezes the other letters into its middle

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it, so managed gives ran

indicators.note: only the inside letters of the word down are used

explanation.surface: Someone manages to wriggle down inside a hollow tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' is neither direction nor feathers: only its middle is used.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain ash, with red berries, is a familiar species of this name.

clue.text: Surprisingly bone dry if given squeeze, perhaps

indicators.note: the letters fall into a surprising new order

explanation.surface: Wringing out something until it is unexpectedly bone dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squeeze' looks like wringing, but it is slang for a sweetheart, and 'perhaps' marks the definition as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Main squeeze is informal for a partner, and a male sweetheart is one example.

clue.text: After training, RAF bod is paired with highly decorated flyer

indicators.note: training reshapes, so after it the letters are in a new order

explanation.surface: A trained RAF man, teamed up, becomes a much-decorated airman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'highly decorated flyer' suggests a medal-laden pilot; it is the gaudily plumed bird. RAF is the Royal Air Force; bod is British slang for a person.
explanation.definitionFit: These New Guinea birds have spectacular ornamental plumage, so they are flamboyantly adorned creatures of the air.

clue.text: Female associate embraces current misconception

indicators.note: the outer letters hold the current inside them

parts.note: an ally is an associate
AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: A woman colleague hugs a popular but mistaken idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A fallacy is a mistaken belief, a false notion or error in reasoning.

clue.text: A tree-covered approach? On the contrary

definitions.text: A tree-covered approach? On the contrary

indicators.note: covered signals one piece wrapped around another
this flips the covering, so the tree wraps round the A rather than being covered

parts.note: the fir is a conifer
a way is a route or approach

explanation.surface: A query about an avenue lined with trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' reverses who covers whom: the tree wraps round the A, rather than covering the approach.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf course the mown strip leading to the green is the approach, often lined with trees.

clue.text: One maintains stability, seeing large policeman in grey pants

indicators.note: these letters go inside the scrambled grey
pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters of grey are poorly arranged

parts.note: OS is outsize, the clothing size
a cop is a policeman

explanation.surface: A sighting of a big officer in grey trousers who keeps everyone steady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like trousers but is British slang for rubbish, signalling GYRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinning wheel device used in navigation instruments to hold orientation steady.

clue.text: What may be deposited in Arab banks?

definitions.text: What may be deposited in Arab banks?

indicators.note: the words deposited in Arab hold the letters within them, as a bank holds money

explanation.surface: A question about the money held in Middle Eastern banks.
explanation.walkthrough: The end of 'deposited' with 'in' and the start of 'Arab' spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This currency is used in several Arab states such as Kuwait, Iraq and Jordan, so it is what their banks take in.

clue.text: Resistance has trouble keeping one hidden?

definitions.text: Resistance has trouble keeping one hidden?

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: the trouble word keeps the one inside it

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A wartime underground movement struggles to conceal its transmitter.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the Resistance's secret set, which had to stay concealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Wartime resistance fighters kept wireless transmitters hidden from the occupiers.

clue.text: With regards to fridge being empty, roar over to eating place

parts.note: re means concerning or with regard to

indicators.note: an emptied word keeps only its outside letters
the roar word goes over the little word to, enclosing it

parts.note: to cry is to roar out

explanation.surface: A complaint about an empty fridge, with someone roaring as they head to a café.
explanation.definitionFit: A refectory is a dining hall in a monastery, college or school.

clue.text: Military group has time to request ceasefire at the borders

parts.note: to ask for something is to request it

indicators.note: only the edge letters of the word ceasefire are used

explanation.surface: An army unit has time to seek a truce on the frontiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit assembled for a specific operation, especially in the armed forces.

clue.text: Considers journey that takes in motorway, having a cake to pick up

indicators.note: the journey word takes in the motorway letters

parts.note: a run is a short journey
the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI

indicators.note: in a down clue picking up means the word reads upwards

parts.note: to cake is to set hard

explanation.surface: A traveller on the motorway thinking about stopping for a slice of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pick up' turns SET into TES. The M1 is the London to Leeds motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruminate is to ponder at length, chewing things over.

clue.text: After festival Mick travels around America, listening to this?

definitions.text: After festival Mick travels around America, listening to this?

indicators.note: the rest comes after the festival letters

parts.note: a festival is a fun event, a jollity

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round America
the letters of Mick travel into a new order

explanation.surface: Mick Jagger tours the States after a festival, and the clue asks what he plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travels' makes KMIC from the singer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Funk is the rhythmic, bass-heavy dance genre of James Brown and others.

clue.text: Uplifting verses to include study for vocal part

indicators.note: the reversed verses include the study word
in a down clue lifting up means the verses read upwards

parts.note: odes are poems, verses
to con is to study, an old sense

explanation.surface: Inspiring poems that need some study to be performed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uplifting' looks like praise but reverses ODES to SEDO.
explanation.definitionFit: In a duet, the second or lower line is called by this Italian term.

clue.text: Jammed to Clapton's first hit

indicators.note: the jammed word is attached to that letter
only the opening letter of Clapton is taken

parts.note: something jammed is locked fast

explanation.surface: A jam session leads to Eric Clapton's first chart hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit' looks like a chart record but is the verb, as in to clock someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Clocked is slang for struck someone, especially in the face.

clue.text: Having a heater raised the temperature, though not at first

indicators.note: the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: warmed means heated up

explanation.surface: A heater made the room warmer, though slowly at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heater' looks like a radiator; it is US slang for a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Heater is old gangster slang for a pistol, so carrying one means being equipped with a weapon.

clue.text: EU citizen having right to enter Ulster?

indicators.note: the right letter enters the coat word

parts.note: an ulster is a long loose overcoat

explanation.surface: A European national claims the right to come into Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ulster' looks like Northern Ireland but is a long overcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: Croatia joined the European Union in 2013, so its people are among the bloc's nationals.

clue.text: Procedure held up by involuntary movement of the eye

indicators.note: in a down entry the procedure sits on top of the twitch

parts.note: an op is a surgical procedure
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: An eye operation is delayed by the patient's twitching.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic is the adjective for vision, as in the optic nerve.

clue.text: Roman gods originally included in study of early Europeans

indicators.note: these letters are placed inside the study word

parts.note: to con is to study

indicators.note: originally read as in an original, novel fashion, so the letters take a fresh order

parts.note: the opening letter of gods, as G stands for god in abbreviations

explanation.surface: Roman gods feature in research into prehistoric peoples.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the Roman's name and the god's initial straight would misspell the answer, so 'originally' has to mean freshly arranged as well as first.
explanation.definitionFit: These were the first anatomically modern humans in Europe, of the Upper Palaeolithic.

clue.text: Push dune buggy, essentially getting knackered

indicators.note: knackered is British slang for worn out, so the letters are wrecked into a new order
the essential, central letter of buggy

explanation.surface: Pushing a dune buggy until you are exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes G, the centre of BUGGY, and 'getting knackered' rearranges DUNE plus G.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudge is a gentle shove or prod with the elbow.

clue.text: Our number two admitted being tired

indicators.note: the number two is let in among the other letters

explanation.surface: Our deputy confessed to being exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number two' reads as a deputy, but the two words work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Worn out describes something exhausted or threadbare, no longer fresh.

clue.text: One is foolish, King Edward accepts, to get so closely entwined

indicators.note: the king-and-Edward letters accept the fool inside

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
Ted is a nickname for Edward
a nit is a fool

explanation.surface: King Edward admits being a fool to become closely attached to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Joined or interlaced tightly together, as in a closely bonded community.

clue.text: Your cake lacks regular ingredients — it's horrible!

indicators.note: every second letter of your cake is dropped, leaving the others

explanation.surface: Your cake is missing its usual ingredients, and it tastes awful.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of disgust, as when tasting something revolting.

clue.text: My attempt, ultimately, to send back some old bolts

parts.note: a go is an attempt

indicators.note: sending something back returns it, so the word send runs in the reverse direction
only the final letter of the word to is used
old is abbreviated O, and bolting means running off, so that letter leaves the word some

explanation.surface: A frustrated try at returning some old bolts to the hardware shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bolts' looks like hardware but means runs off. The last letter of 'to' sits before DNES; a lone letter reads the same either way round.
explanation.definitionFit: My! is an exclamation of surprise, as is the fuller expression.
